mechanism_narrative: The slight recovery in RETAIL_REC mobility from t-1w to t-0w, after a period of decline, indicates a nascent upward trend in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation footfall higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility falls below -8.0% in any of the next four weeks, reversing the observed recovery.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in PARKS mobility from -25.9% at t-1w to -15.7% at t-0w suggests an increasing public willingness to engage in outdoor leisure. If this trend continues, it will positively influence broader retail and recreation activities over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls or stagnates (rises by less than 2 percentage points) in the next week, indicating a halt in outdoor activity recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Currently high RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with low WORKPLACES mobility indicates people are largely staying home. A simultaneous and sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals a return to out-of-home routines, which will boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by 2+ points and RESIDENTIAL falls by 1+ point for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility continues to fall or RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to rise, indicating no shift from stay-at-home patterns.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently low TRANSIT mobility, hovering around -24% to -26% over the last four weeks, suggests ongoing public apprehension or official restrictions on movement. This sustained suppression of public transport use will continue to limit access to and engagement with retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 10 percentage points from its current level within the next two weeks, indicating a significant easing of movement constraints.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has shown a steady increase, indicating comfort with essential outings. If this trend plateaus or declines, it suggests a general reduction in all out-of-home activities, including non-essential retail and recreation, over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls week-on-week or rises by less than 0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues its upward trend, rising by more than 0.5 percentage points in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized dip at t-1w and subsequent recovery at t-0w in both PARKS and RETAIL_REC mobility suggests a shared underlying driver for leisure activities. If PARKS mobility continues its recovery trajectory, RETAIL_REC will follow suit over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises for two consecutive weeks, each by at least 3 percentage points
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises as predicted, but RETAIL_REC mobility falls or remains stagnant (changes by less than 1 percentage point).

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained consistently low and stagnant, averaging around -8% over the last four weeks. This sustained lack of return to office work indicates a continued suppression of weekday retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility shows a sustained increase of more than 2 percentage points over two consecutive weeks, indicating a shift in work patterns.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility, consistently above baseline at +3% to +4%, indicates ongoing stay-at-home directives or strong public adherence to them. This will continue to directly limit opportunities for out-of-home retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below baseline (0%) for two consecutive weeks, suggesting a significant relaxation of stay-at-home behavior.
